newsitem.title: USA: Arrest in killing that raised Philadelphia tensions.
newsitem.headline: Arrest in killing that raised Philadelphia tensions.

text.p: Police said Tuesday they had arrested a suspect in connection with the killing of a teenager that has fanned racial tensions in a working class city neighbourhood.

City police homicide Capt. James Brady told reporters 20-year-old Al Thomas was arrested Tuesday morning and charged with murder and other crimes in connection with the killing of Christopher Brinkman, 16, the son of a Philadelphia policeman, in a drug store robbery last Friday.
Another suspect, believed to have been the gunman in the incident, surrendered to police Tuesday afternoon, but his identity could not immediately be confirmed, police said.
Both suspects are black, while Brinkman was white.

The killing, in the Grays Ferry neighbourhood of south Philadelphia, heightened racial tensions in the area. Relations have been tense since a Feb. 22 beating of black woman, allegedly by a group of 20 to 50 white men emerging from a party. Two men have been arrested in the beatings.
The Nation of Islam said Monday it would hold a march of 5,000 men through the neighbourhood April 14, seeking an end to violence.
At a funeral service for the slain youth Monday evening at St. Gabriel's Roman Catholic church, Rev. Ronald Rossi issued a plea for calm on behalf of the boy's parents.

"Tell the community enough blood has been shed," he said, quoting the parents. "Tell the community we don't want to see another parent of any race ... go through the pain, the grief and the suffering we've gone through."

Thomas was arrested after he went to a city police station with local radio journalist Larry Kane. Thomas contacted Kane late Monday and said in an interview with Kane, broadcast on KYW-AM radio, that he wanted to clear his name after hearing rumours he was wanted for questioning.
"He was very nervous about coming to the police station alone, which I told him wouldn't be a problem," Kane said.
